high.title: Government Directs SBV to Study Increasing Banking System Liquidity via State Treasury Deposits
high.summary:
The Vietnamese Government issued Resolution 168/NQ-CP on June 27, 2026, updating growth scenarios and key solutions for the remaining quarters of 2026, with an ambitious GDP growth target of 10% or above alongside maintaining macroeconomic stability. Critically, the Government has directed the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) to study and explore channeling State Treasury deposits into the banking system as a mechanism to boost liquidity. This is a significant policy signal for fixed income and FX traders: injecting Treasury deposits into commercial banks would expand system liquidity, placing downward pressure on interbank lending rates and potentially on deposit rates over time. It could also reduce the need for SBV open market operations (OMO). The Government acknowledged global headwinds — particularly Middle East conflicts — impacting the economy in H1 2026, yet cited strong macro indicators. For bond investors, increased liquidity could compress short-end government bond yields. For VND, the net effect depends on execution; excessive easing could introduce mild depreciation pressure. **Watch:** SBV's formal response and any OMO adjustments in coming sessions.

---

high.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of June 29: ACB Leads Market at 7.3%/year for 12-Month Tenor; State-Owned Banks Hold at 6.8%/year
high.summary:
As Vietnam enters the final days of June, the retail deposit rate landscape has stabilized with no major adjustments recorded. The survey of rates on June 29 shows ACB maintaining market leadership at 7.3%/year for 12-month online deposits — the sole institution above the 7.2% threshold for that tenor. ACB also posts 7.1%/year for 6-month and 7.2%/year for 9-month terms. Saigonbank ranks second at 7.2%/year for 12 months and 7.0% for 18 months. MBV, PGBank, VCBNeo, and VIB all sit at 7.0%/year for 12-month deposits, bringing the total number of banks at or above 7.0% to six institutions. The large state-owned banks (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) remain anchored at 6.8%/year. **Market relevance:** The persistence of elevated private bank deposit rates at 7.0–7.3% signals continued competition for liquidity and could put upward pressure on lending rates, constraining credit growth. The divergence between state-owned and private bank rates warrants monitoring as a leading indicator of system-wide funding stress. Bond investors should watch whether higher deposit rates begin to crowd out demand for government paper at current yield levels.

---

high.title: Fubon FTSE Vietnam ETF Records Net Outflows for 10 Consecutive Quarters
high.summary: The Fubon FTSE Vietnam ETF — the largest foreign ETF invested in Vietnamese equities with assets of approximately 14.65 billion TWD (~VND 12,000 billion) — has now recorded net outflows for 10 consecutive quarters, representing the longest sustained redemption streak since the fund's entry into the Vietnamese market. After strong inflows during 2022 and the first half of 2023, sentiment fully reversed beginning Q3/2023, with no single quarter posting positive net flows since. In Q2/2026 alone, net outflows reached approximately 3.28 billion TWD (~VND 2,700 billion), indicating a meaningful acceleration in redemption pressure. The fund holds a concentrated 30-stock portfolio (99.2% invested) skewed toward large-cap, high-liquidity blue chips on the VN-Index.

medium.title: MBS: History Shows the World Cup Season Is Not a Golden Period for the Stock Market
medium.summary: MB Securities (MBS) notes that the Vietnamese equity market is recovering toward the 1,900-point level on the VN-Index, but the rally is described as superficial — for every stock rising, approximately five are declining, creating a significant divergence between index performance and actual portfolio outcomes. Market liquidity remains weak, though MBS flags that this weakness is occurring in the absence of negative global market catalysts and that foreign net selling pressure has meaningfully moderated. The brokerage identifies a key paradox: money flows appear excessively cautious and indifferent despite a series of foundational macro policy pivots that are underway. MBS argues these policies will not produce immediate results but will compound over time as infrastructure projects accelerate and structural bottlenecks are resolved. **Relevance for fund managers:** The moderation in foreign net selling is a positive signal worth monitoring for potential capital flow reversal into Vietnamese equities. Continued thin liquidity, however, suggests foreign investors remain in a wait-and-see posture on VN-Index positioning.

medium.title: LPBank Securities (LPBS) to List on HoSE Following IPO Completion
medium.summary: LPBank Securities (LPBS) has announced the record date for its shareholder list (closing at 5:00 PM on June 29, 2026) as part of procedures to register shares with the Vietnam Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation (VSDC) and pursue a listing on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HoSE). The listing follows the completion of LPBS's IPO. Notable among major shareholders are children of prominent businessman "Bầu Thụy." **Relevance for fund managers:** A new securities firm listing on HoSE marginally expands the investable universe and may attract incremental liquidity to the exchange. As an affiliate of LPBank, this also has peripheral relevance to the Vietnamese banking sector's capital market expansion, though direct impact on VND or bond markets is limited.

medium.title: Top 15 Largest Companies in Southeast Asia: Vingroup and Vinhomes Make the List, Surpassing Names from Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia
medium.summary:
According to data compiled by CompaniesMarketCap, Vingroup has risen to 4th place in Southeast Asia with a market capitalization of approximately USD 65 billion (~VND 1.7 quadrillion), while its subsidiary Vinhomes also entered the top 15 at USD 25 billion. This places Vingroup ahead of regional blue-chips including Singtel, Sea Limited, Flex, and UOB. Singapore's DBS Group retains the top spot at USD 144 billion, followed by Delta Electronics of Thailand (USD 114 billion) and OCBC Bank of Singapore. For international fund managers, this development highlights the growing weight and maturity of the Vietnamese equity market on a regional scale. The rising market cap of Vingroup entities could attract incremental passive and active foreign inflows into Vietnamese equities, potentially supporting the VN-Index and providing mild tailwinds for VND demand from foreign investors. This is a useful reference point for assessing Vietnam's relative position in regional EM allocation decisions.

---

medium.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of June 28 — Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank and Others
medium.summary: A survey of online deposit rate schedules across 34 Vietnamese banks as of June 28 shows the interest rate environment remains broadly stable with limited movement. The majority of banks are quoting 12-month deposit rates in the 6.8–6.9% per annum range, with only six banks offering rates at or above the 7% threshold. ACB leads the market at 7.3% p.a. for 12-month deposits, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2% p.a. Other banks at the 7% level for 12-month tenors include MBV, PGBank, VCBNeo, and VIB. The overall stability of deposit rates suggests no immediate shift in monetary conditions, though the Government's push for higher growth and increased liquidity (see Article 3) bears watching for any second-half rate adjustments. For bond investors, sticky deposit rates in the 6.8–7.3% band continue to set a floor for government bond yield expectations across short-to-medium tenors.

medium.title: New Personal Income Tax on Gold Bar Trading Effective July 1, 2026
medium.summary: Effective July 1, 2026, the Personal Income Tax Law 2025 (Law No. 109/2025/QH15), passed by the National Assembly in December 2025, comes into force. A key new provision classifies income from gold bar (vàng miếng) transfers as taxable income under Article 3. The Government retains authority to set the taxable threshold, effective date, and applicable tax rate in line with the broader gold market management roadmap. For non-resident individuals, PIT on gold transfer income is calculated based on the transfer price. This regulatory tightening is part of Vietnam's ongoing effort to formalize and regulate the domestic gold market. For FX and macro traders, this matters as domestic gold demand dynamics influence USD/VND pressure — gold imports have historically been a notable source of dollar demand. Reduced speculative gold trading activity could marginally ease USD demand, providing modest support to VND. **Watch:** Government decree specifying the tax threshold and rate, and any impact on SJC/gold market volumes.

medium.title: Advice for Investors Who Bought Gold at the Peak of VND 180 Million/Tael
medium.summary: Gold prices in Vietnam have entered a sharp correction phase following a period of elevated gains, with domestic gold reaching approximately VND 180 million/tael before pulling back. The correction is being driven by a stronger USD and Federal Reserve signals that interest rates may remain elevated for longer — both classic headwinds for gold. An analyst from FIDT notes that 60–70% of gold price movements can currently be explained by USD dynamics, with the traditional inverse relationship intact. This article is relevant to VND traders as it highlights the strength of the USD, which simultaneously pressures both gold and VND. The Fed's hawkish posture, if sustained, could extend USD strength and add depreciation pressure on the Dong in the near term. Domestic gold price dynamics also reflect Vietnamese investor sentiment toward inflation hedging and currency risk, which can feed back into broader capital flow patterns.

medium.title: SBV Governor Pham Duc An Attends BIS Annual General Meeting 2026
medium.summary: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) Governor Pham Duc An led a delegation to the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Annual General Meeting in 2026. The BIS approved its Annual Report and financial statements for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026, alongside key governance resolutions. The BIS Annual Economic Report noted that the global economy passed through two contrasting phases over the past year: initial resilience driven by AI investment and favorable financial conditions, followed by a significant supply-side shock stemming from the Hormuz Strait crisis that impacted energy markets from early 2026. Based on this assessment, the BIS recommended that central banks shift focus from short-term resilience management toward building durable long-term foundations. **Relevance:** Governor An's participation signals Vietnam's continued engagement with the global central banking community. The BIS warning on energy-driven supply shocks is pertinent for Vietnam's inflation outlook and SBV's monetary policy calculus, particularly given Vietnam's energy import exposure. Fund managers should monitor whether the Hormuz crisis narrative influences SBV's rate-setting posture in H2 2026.

medium.title: Vietnam's Banking Profit Rankings After a Decade: Vietcombank Claims the Top Spot, HDBank and LPBank Rise Sharply
medium.summary: A retrospective analysis of Vietnamese banking sector profitability over the past decade reveals significant structural shifts. Vietcombank has risen from third place in 2015 (pre-tax profit of VND 6,828 billion) to the undisputed sector leader in 2025, with pre-tax profit of VND 44,020 billion — the first Vietnamese bank to surpass the VND 44,000 billion milestone. This ascent came at the expense of BIDV and VietinBank, which previously alternated as the top earners. Vietcombank's success is attributed to asset quality discipline, retail banking expansion, funding cost control, and operational efficiency rather than pure credit volume growth. Notably, HDBank and LPBank have shown impressive upward mobility in the rankings, while one unnamed institution dropped 10 places. **Relevance for investors:** Vietcombank's dominance reinforces its status as the highest-quality credit in the Vietnamese banking sector. The rising profitability of HDBank and LPBank may attract incremental equity flows. For bond and FX investors, healthy bank profitability supports system stability and reduces the likelihood of SBV being forced into emergency liquidity interventions.

medium.title: VPBank Signs Its First Sustainability-Linked Syndicated Loan Worth $1.44 Billion USD
medium.summary: VPBank signed a 3-year sustainability-linked syndicated loan (SLL) on June 30, 2026, with 15 major international financial institutions present at the signing ceremony in Hanoi. The loan was upsized from an initial $1.2 billion to $1.44 billion USD (~VND 37,900 billion), reflecting strong appetite from global lenders. The facility is structured around Sustainability Performance Targets (SPTs), with financial terms tied to VPBank's annual progress in expanding green and social lending portfolios. This represents a significant inflow of foreign capital into Vietnam's banking sector and signals growing international confidence in Vietnamese financial institutions. For FX markets, the USD inflow at this scale could provide modest near-term support to VND liquidity conditions and eases funding pressure on one of Vietnam's largest private banks.
